name: p2-2007-mac-vs-gnu
title: Same one-liner, different answer on Mac and Ubuntu
spec: A comparison table with three columns: 'Command', 'On the Mac' (grey header) and 'On Ubuntu with GNU tools' (green header). Rows drawn as cards, with commands in monospace. Row 1: "date -d '2026-03-12' +%F" | 'illegal option -- d' (red text) | '2026-03-12' (green text). Row 2: 'stat -c %s file' | 'illegal option -- c' | '4 for a four-byte file'. Row 3: 'echo -n | xargs echo hi' | 'printed nothing' | 'printed hi, add -r to stop that'. Row 4: 'sed -i s/x/y/ file' | 'needs a suffix argument' | 'works without one'. Row 5: '((i++)) under set -e with i=0' | 'script did not stop on bash 3.2' | 'script stops with exit 1 on bash 5.2.21'. Row 6: "grep -oP '\d+'" | 'not available in the BSD grep' | 'prints each number'. Row 7: 'default awk' | 'one true awk, 20200816' | 'mawk 1.3.4 on a fresh Ubuntu'. Orange outline on the xargs row as the silent-failure trap. Bottom green bar: 'Write POSIX pipelines and say aloud when you use a GNU extension.'
anchor: ### 3. The Mac is not the interview box
alt: A table of commands that behave differently on macOS and on Ubuntu with GNU tools, such as date, stat, xargs, sed and the default awk.
cap: Commands that behave differently on a Mac and on Ubuntu with GNU tools, so a one-liner that works on a laptop can fail on the interview box.

name: p2-2007-pid1-init
title: PID 1 without a handler ignores TERM
spec: Two side-by-side panels with green headings. Left panel 'Container with sleep as PID 1': a container box with a PID 1 chip labelled 'sleep', a status card 'SigCgt: all zeros (no handlers)', and a timer bar labelled 'docker stop -t 4: 4.1 seconds, whole grace period, then SIGKILL' in orange outline. Right panel 'Same container with --init': a container box with a PID 1 chip labelled 'docker-init', a timer bar labelled 'docker stop: 0.1 seconds'. Under the left panel a small zombie row labelled 'Children never reaped: zombies pile up'. Under the right panel a note 'docker run --init adds an init process as PID 1'. Bottom caption: 'PID 1 in a container ignores signals it has no handler for.'
alt: Two containers compared: one with sleep as PID 1 that takes the full four-second grace period to stop, and one started with an init process that stops in 0.1 seconds.
cap: A container whose PID 1 has no signal handler takes the whole grace period to stop, while a container started with an init process stops at once.

name: p2-2007-restart-loop
title: A restart loop hits the start limit
spec: A horizontal cycle drawn as four boxes in a loop with arrows: 'Process starts and does its setup', 'Setup fails: exit status', 'systemd waits RestartSec=100ms', 'Restart counter goes up by one', with an arrow looping back to the first box. Next to the loop, a fence-like gate labelled 'StartLimitIntervalSec and StartLimitBurst: too many tries too fast'. An arrow from the loop to the gate, and from the gate to a red-outlined box 'Unit marked failed, not restarted any more'. Below the failed box a green command chip in monospace 'systemctl reset-failed'. Right side, a small read-order card titled 'Read in order': '1. exit status line', '2. restart counter', '3. the limit', '4. only then change Restart='. Orange outline on the 'Unit marked failed' box. Caption: 'Changing the restart policy first hides the crash you need to understand.'
alt: A restart loop in which a service fails and is restarted every 100 milliseconds until the start limit marks the unit failed.
cap: A restart loop that crosses the start limit marks the unit as failed, so read the exit status and counter before changing the restart policy.

name: p2-2007-curl-exit
title: curl without -f exits zero on a 404
spec: Two parallel run boxes, each a terminal-style panel with monospace text. Left panel titled 'curl without -f': command line 'curl ... missing page' followed by output 'status 404' and an exit status chip 'exit code 0' in a green outline with a warning note 'the script sees success'. Right panel titled 'curl with -f': the same command with the flag '-f' added, output with no body, and an exit status chip 'exit code 22' in an orange outline with the note 'set -e stops the script'. Between the two panels a bridge arrow labelled 'Same request, same 404'. Bottom note: 'In scripts, the exit code is the only thing set -e sees.'
anchor: ### 9. tar, rsync, curl and jq one-liners
alt: The same request for a missing page exits zero without the fail flag and exits twenty-two with it, which changes whether a script stops.
cap: A missing page returns exit code 0 from curl by default and exit code 22 with the fail flag, so only the second stops a script.
